solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Units of precious material bringing a certain uneasiness

definitions.meaning: ... were apothecaries' units of weight of twenty grains, used for measuring out costly drugs
qualms of conscience, a nagging doubt about whether something is right

explanation.surface: Small measures of something valuable bring with them a nagging sense of unease.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard dictionary senses: an old apothecaries' weight, and the moral hesitation that holds a person back.

clue.text: Behold this person, with it at the outset, as dancer

parts.note: it is SA, sex appeal; at the outset says it goes at the front
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
me is the setter, this person

explanation.surface: Look at me, with sex appeal from the start, as a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' = SA (sex appeal) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Salome is the biblical figure who danced the Dance of the Seven Veils for Herod.

clue.text: Don is one person trying hard, but no saint

indicators.note: no means the saint is removed

parts.note: a striver is someone who tries hard

explanation.surface: An Oxford don is a diligent worker but certainly no saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' suggests a university lecturer; it is the Don, a river in Russia (and several in Britain).
explanation.definitionFit: The Don is a river, so it is an example of the answer's category.

clue.text: Tireless individual not getting on is behind nine others, falling short

indicators.note: not getting means the following word is removed from the individual

parts.note: an individual is a person
taken as written

indicators.note: falling short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: one who comes behind nine others is tenth

explanation.surface: A tireless person who isn't getting on trails nine others, missing the target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting on' cuts PERSON to PERS; 'falling short' trims TENTH to TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent means continuing firmly despite obstacles, never tiring of the effort.

clue.text: There's not much money here when person has lost pounds

indicators.note: has lost means the pounds letter is taken away

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in not a soul
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: There is little money about once someone has lost a lot of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' looks like weight lost on a diet; it is L, pounds sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou was a French coin of low value, so it stands for a trifling amount of money.

clue.text: Prison room chipped with insertion of the chap's carpentry tool

indicators.note: insertion means the next piece is put inside the shortened room
chipped means a bit is knocked off the end, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cell is a room in a prison
the chap's means his

explanation.surface: A prisoner chips away at a cell wall using a woodworking blade he has smuggled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chipped' removes the last L of the room; 'with insertion of' puts the chap's word inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A chisel is a bladed hand tool that woodworkers use to cut and shape timber.

clue.text: Show disapproval? It's conveyed by this sound

indicators.note: conveyed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sound that expresses disapproval is said to carry it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'It's', but the verb definition is only 'Show disapproval'; 'It's' points to the sound, a semi-all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences hiss to express their displeasure at a villain or poor performance.

clue.text: Parade's given order, gathered round explosive leader

indicators.note: gathered round means the rearranged letters go around the explosive
given order means the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: Troops are ordered on parade and gather round a leader with explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given order' rearranges the letters into SPEARAD; 'gathered round' wraps that around high explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: The spearhead is the person or group leading an attack or campaign.

clue.text: Like many words derived from province dad's not used

indicators.note: not used means dad is left out of the province

parts.note: a palatinate is a province ruled by a count palatine, as in the German Palatinate
pa is dad; dad's here means dad is

explanation.surface: Words come from a province where the father's language is no longer spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Latinate means derived from or resembling Latin, as much English vocabulary is.

clue.text: Organ of bird seen in northern city

definitions.meaning: a large organ of the body that cleans the blood
the ... bird is the mythical bird that stands on the Royal ... Building as the emblem of Liverpool

explanation.surface: A bird's internal organ is examined in a city in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liver bird is the cormorant-like emblem of Liverpool, a city in north-west England; 'of' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is the body organ; the second is the name of the bird that symbolises Liverpool.

clue.text: Stop to absorb English view, shortly resting

indicators.note: to absorb means the stopping word takes the following letters into itself

parts.note: to quit is to stop

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a scene is a view

explanation.surface: Someone stops to take in an English view and rests for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the view's final E; 'to absorb' takes English and the shortened view into the stopping word.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiescent describes something inactive or dormant, at rest for the moment.

clue.text: To rave in front of eyewitness in court gets one detained

indicators.note: in court means the pieces go inside the courtyard word

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard
to rant is to rave

indicators.note: front of means take the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Raging at a witness in the courtroom gets you locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' looks like one phrase: split it, with the first 'in' taken as written and 'front of' picking E. The second 'in' puts everything inside the courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quarantined is held in isolation to stop the spread of disease, so is confined.

clue.text: Maybe painter otherwise challenged avoids a tint that's unusual

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An unusual artist dodges a particular colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes someone with a learning disability who shows extraordinary talent in one field, such as art.

clue.text: Notes from girl in show imbibing drink with gangster?

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the girl's name holds the next pieces

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of the musical West Side Story (and of The Sound of Music)
gin is a drink
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Notes from a stage heroine who drinks with a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibing' puts the drink and the gangster inside the girl's name; Maria is the heroine of West Side Story.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginalia are the jottings and comments written in the margins of a book.

clue.text: Grimace to show vexation when tea is not provided

indicators.note: not provided means the tea is left out of the vexed word

parts.note: chagrin is vexation or annoyance at a failure
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face in annoyance because no tea has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not provided' takes CHA off the front of CHAGRIN. A grin can be a fixed, strained baring of the teeth, a grimace.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin bares the teeth, and a forced or pained one is a kind of grimace.

clue.text: A group performing, one no good, giving up

parts.note: a band is a musical group
a performer on stage is on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A group on stage, one of them hopeless, decides to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning means deserting or relinquishing, as when one stops an attempt.

clue.text: Transporter returned piece of furniture that could be shrunk for packing?

definitions.text: that could be shrunk for packing?

indicators.note: returned means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a carter transports goods by cart
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A removal man brings back a table that folds down to fit in the van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns CARTER into RETRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something retractable can be drawn in or pulled back, so it takes up less space when stowed.

clue.text: Dissenters demonstrating a curtness, being put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dissenters show a curt manner when they are annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Recusants were people who refused to attend Church of England services, so religious nonconformists.

clue.text: 5-5? Come on!

indicators.note: the minus sign between the two fives says one is taken away from the other

parts.note: the figure 5 written out as a word
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue followed by an impatient exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a pointer to 5 across, but has nothing to do with it: the dash is a minus, removing Roman V from the word FIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fie is an old exclamation of reproach or disgust, like an exasperated 'Come on!'

clue.text: What may be marked with a D in paper

definitions.text: What may be marked with a D
definitions.meaning: a dunce's hat, the cone a slow pupil was made to wear, often lettered with a D
a traditional large size of writing or printing paper

explanation.surface: A schoolroom dunce's cap made of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as FOOL'S CAP it is the dunce's hat; as one word it is a paper size.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a paper size of about 13 by 16 inches; the fool's cap is the dunce's conical hat.

clue.text: Vote for a second person that's old-fashioned

parts.note: ye is the archaic second-person pronoun meaning you

explanation.surface: Someone casts a vote for a runner-up who is rather old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye is the word for yes when a vote is called, as in Parliament, so it is a vote in favour.

clue.text: Prisoners given exercises kept within bounds

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts
someone trained has been put through exercises

explanation.surface: Inmates put through their drills are kept within the prison limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Constrained means restricted or held in check, kept within limits.

clue.text: Ward in which church is guarded

indicators.note: in which means the church goes inside the warding word

parts.note: to ward off is to fend off
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A hospital ward containing a chapel is kept under guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ward' suggests a hospital room; it is the verb ward (off), FEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenced means enclosed by a barrier and so protected.

clue.text: Bathroom's flowing water not fine for drinker

indicators.note: not means the fine letter is removed from the flush

parts.note: a flush is the rush of water through a lavatory
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A toilet's water isn't good enough for a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush is slang for a heavy drinker or alcoholic.

clue.text: Social worker dealt with worry and anger

parts.note: an ant is a social insect and a worker ant toils for the colony
to agonise is to worry intensely

explanation.surface: A social worker handles a case of worry and anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a council caseworker; here it is an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise someone is to provoke their hostility, making them annoyed.

clue.text: Successful person, not the first in a sporting circle

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a winner is a successful person

explanation.surface: A victor, not the first in some sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting circle' suggests a social set; it is the ring next to the bull on an archery or shooting target.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target the inner is the ring just outside the bull, a scoring circle.

clue.text: Something aromatic upsetting university group

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the letters upside down, reading them from the bottom

parts.note: a lot is a group, as in that lot

explanation.surface: Something fragrant upsets a university group.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolu is a fragrant balsam from a South American tree, used in medicines and perfume.

clue.text: Agreement about material getting snagged by puss

indicators.note: snagged by means caught inside the cat's letters

parts.note: puss is a cat
on means about or concerning
cord is a ribbed fabric, corduroy

explanation.surface: An agreement concerning fabric that the cat has caught its claws in.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially one between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Martyr casting off an ecclesiastical garment

indicators.note: casting off means the following word is shed from the martyr's name

parts.note: St Alban was the first British Christian martyr

explanation.surface: A martyr removes a church vestment.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is a long white vestment worn by clergy at the Eucharist.

clue.text: Greek philosopher using Socratic method, brooking no resistance

indicators.note: brooking no means not tolerating, so the resistance letter is dropped

parts.note: Socratic irony is feigned ignorance used to draw out an opponent, so such a philosopher is being ironic
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A Greek thinker questioning in the Socratic manner tolerates no opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek' looks like it describes the philosopher, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the ancient Greek dialects and orders of architecture, so it means of Ionia in Greece.

clue.text: Refuse drink after juice has been sent back

indicators.note: after puts the drink behind the juice
sent back means the juice word is turned round

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone declines a drink because the juice was returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been sent back' turns SAP into PAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an offer is to decline or turn down the opportunity.

clue.text: Bothered and embarrassed by commercial label

indicators.note: by puts the embarrassed word beside, after, the label

parts.note: a badge is an emblem or brand, as in badge engineering of cars
an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: Someone is bothered and embarrassed by a brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: Badgered means pestered or harassed repeatedly, made bothered.
